TASK.md is authoritative on WHAT, SPEC.md on HOW. Deadline is Saturday 15 Aug, so scope
discipline matters more than completeness.

Do NOT write any application code in this turn.

Four things:

1. LOGGING CHECK — first, confirm the prompt-logging hook is working. Tell me whether
   PROMPTS.jsonl gained a line for this prompt. If it did not, diagnose and fix the
   hooks for macOS before anything else, then confirm again. This is a hard blocker:
   the log is part of the submission.

2. CRITIQUE THE SPEC — read SPEC.md properly and push back. I want disagreement, not
   validation. Specifically:

     under-specified to the point where you'd have to guess while implementing.

   Next skeleton + Postgres + Drizzle + lib/schema/, per SPEC.md §11). Include the exact
   verification step for each task — how I'll know it actually works, not just that the
   file exists.

Then stop and wait. I'll approve the plan before you build anything.

Also, the directory you're working in is supposed to be a git repository, so check if it is and that's where you'll be commiting your work. DO NOT DO git init, DO NOT DELETE the existing .git folder, you need to commit to the existing folder.

Type check passes.

**Cause:** the route passed `onEnd` to `toUIMessageStream`, but per the v7 notes `onEnd` is `streamText`'s own callback name (final-step-only, tool-loop-blind) while `toUIMessageStream`'s callback is `onFinish` — since `toUIMessageStream` doesn't recognize `onEnd`, persistence never ran off the accumulated UI message that actually contains the tool-* parts from earlier steps. prompt:
Read @app/layout.tsx, @app/globals.css, @app/page.tsx,
@app/components/PlanPanel.tsx, @app/settings/page.tsx and
@app/profile/page.tsx.

Task: a visual redesign only. This app currently looks like an unstyled
Next.js scaffold — near-black, default type, no hierarchy. Give it a warm,
calm, editorial identity suited to trip planning: something a person would
be happy to sit in for an hour while shaping a holiday.

## Hard constraints — do not violate

- Change presentation only. Do NOT touch lib/, app/api/, any Zod schema,
  any tool, or any data flow.
- Preserve exactly: streaming behaviour and useChat wiring, the plan panel's
  optimistic updates and 409 handling, the locked-item indicator and its
  tooltip, the rejected-ops notice, the read-only composed prompt block on
  the settings page, and every existing link and button action.
- Tailwind v4 — define tokens with @theme in globals.css, not a
  tailwind.config.js.
- Markdown is rendered with streamdown. Style its output; do not replace it.
- No new dependencies except lucide-react.
- No logo, wordmark, or naming that implies affiliation with any AI vendor.

## Design tokens

Define these in @theme and use them everywhere. No raw hex outside this block.

  --color-paper:    #FBF9F6   /* page ground, warm off-white */
  --color-surface:  #FFFFFF   /* cards, panel, input                */
  --color-line:     #E8E2D9   /* hairline borders, dividers         */
  --color-ink:      #22201D   /* primary text                       */
  --color-muted:    #6E675E   /* secondary text, labels, timestamps */
  --color-accent:   #3F6E5A   /* deep pine — actions, active state, links */
  --color-accent-soft: #EDF2EF /* accent tint for active rows        */
  --color-warn:     #A8563C   /* rejected ops, destructive confirm   */

The accent is a muted deep green rather than the terracotta that is currently
ubiquitous in AI-generated interfaces. Keep it restrained: it appears on the
active conversation, primary buttons, focus rings and links, and nowhere else.

## Typography

- Body and UI: keep Geist Sans, already loaded via next/font.
- Display: add ONE serif via next/font/google for headings, the app title,
  the trip title and day labels in the plan panel. Use Newsreader — it is
  warm and readable without the high-contrast editorial look that reads as
  a template. Load only the weights used.
- Scale: 13px labels / 15px body / 17px chat message / 20px section heads /
  28px page title. Body line-height 1.6. Chat messages capped at ~68ch.
- Numbers in the plan (times, costs, nights) use tabular figures.

## Screens

**Chat (app/page.tsx).** Three columns on desktop: conversation list, chat,
plan panel. The list is quiet — title, relative timestamp, accent-soft
background on the active row. User messages sit right in a soft accent-tinted
bubble; assistant messages sit left on paper with no bubble at all, so they
read as prose rather than chat. Give the composer a clear resting state, a
visible focus ring, and a disabled state while streaming. Style streamdown
output properly: headings, lists, bold, and links should all have deliberate
spacing rather than browser defaults.

**Plan panel.** This is the artifact the whole app produces — it should feel
like a document, not a sidebar. Trip title in the serif. Destinations, dates,
party and budget as a compact summary strip. Days as sections with a serif
label; items as rows with a small lucide icon per kind (activity, food,
transport, lodging, note). Locked items get a subtle lock icon and a faint
accent left border — legible without shouting. Open questions get their own
block at the bottom, visually distinct from decided content.

**Settings and profile.** Same shell and type scale. The read-only composed
prompt stays monospace on a slightly recessed surface. Destructive buttons
use --color-warn and keep their existing confirm step.

**Empty states.** Replace anything blank with one short line that says what
to do next, in plain sentence case. "No trip yet — tell the advisor where
you're going." Not "No data available."

## Icons

lucide-react only, 16px in rows and 18px in headers, stroke 1.5, always with
an aria-label or adjacent text. Do not decorate — an icon appears only where
it identifies something (item kind, locked state, delete, new conversation).

## Quality floor

Responsive down to 390px, where the plan panel becomes a tab rather than a
column. Visible keyboard focus on every interactive element. Respect
prefers-reduced-motion. Transitions no longer than 150ms and only on hover
and focus — no entrance animations.

## When done

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test`, then list every file you changed and
state in one line what you did NOT touch.

Work in this session only. No subagents, no background workflows.
One task, then stop.
